what: AnyJev Tacitus 31B, a decision model fine-tuned from google/gemma-4-31B-it and read with AnyJev, on the Decision Index 0.4.1 board
weights: bf16 on the Hub (commit 616d514); FP8 by vLLM's dynamic quantization at load (--quantization fp8)

readout.serving: vLLM 0.29.0 with the model's vLLM plugin (anyjev-vllm-bidi)

public_run.server: vLLM 0.29.0, torch 2.13.0+cu129, --quantization fp8, --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs, prefix caching on, TRITON_ATTN, max-model-len 114688
public_run.hardware: NVIDIA H100 NVL (94 GB); the suite was split over two identical tensor-parallel-2 servers

board.name: AnyJev Tacitus 31B

latency_ms.measured_by: the board's maintainers, single process on one RTX PRO 6000, private held-out sample

maintainer_notes: Submitted public 0.3 run adopted (kit rescore 65.52, equal to the claim). Private tests run by the lab on one RTX PRO 6000 with the author's serving (FP8 at load); decision agreement with the submitted rows 98.29% on 827 rows (bar 96%).
A separate model from AnyJev L0 · Gemma-4-31B, which stays on the board.
Served in FP8 at load as in the submitted run, so the quantized agreement bar applies.
Run with a 32,768-token context window on one card; the author used 114,688 across four GPUs.
Per-benchmark times are not shown: the board run sent requests in batches, so its timings are batch wall-clock. The latency shown is the single-request measurement.
